newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STARTS FRIDAY MIXED IN LOW TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STARTS FRIDAY MIXED IN LOW TRADE.

text.p: Zimbabwe's interbank foreign exchange market opened quietly on Friday in the aftermath of Thursday's buying spree to finance a big payment, with the local unit quoted mixed against major currencies.
"I think all the excitement of the (U.S.$10 million) payment is now gone. We opened where we closed yesterday and we haven't moved a cent since then," one exchange dealer said.
He added however: "But the market is about U.S.$1.5 million short and in view of this we might see the Zimbabwe dollar go to yesterday's peaks later."

At around 0735 GMT, the local unit was trading unchanged from its overnight levels at 10.9550/9700 against the key U.S. dollar but firmed to 17.6430/6730 from 17.7510/7880 versus pound sterling, tracking a stronger U.S. dollar overseas.
It was however quoted softer on the mark at 6.6890/7020 compared to 6.6750/6880 and slipped to 2.4000/4050 from 2.3970/4030 against South Africa's rand.
